minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard FY19 budget presentations from cable access, Monty Tech, schools, DPW and sewer; no votes
minutes.summary: The committee heard budget presentations from the public access cable committee, Monty Tech, the Lunenburg schools, the DPW director and the sewer commission. Questions came after seven o'clock because of a posting error. The schools presented a level-service budget voted by the School Committee, and the sewer commission said its budget was not yet balanced. The town accountant reviewed the warrant articles. No formal votes were recorded.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY19 budget presentations from cable access, Monty Tech, the schools, DPW and the sewer commission, and took no votes.
The sewer commission said its budget is not balanced, citing a revenue error and cost increases from Fitchburg, and will rebalance it the following Tuesday.
The schools presented a level-service budget as voted by the School Committee, with a possible Title I loss handled through flexibility rather than layoffs.
Monty Tech's proposed budget rises, but Lunenburg's assessment goes down because enrollment fell.
Discussion of the large capital item spreadsheet was pushed to a later meeting.

why_it_matters: The sewer budget is not yet balanced, so sewer rates or the town's share of the cost could still change before Town Meeting.
School and Monty Tech figures set part of the tax bill, and the school budget depends on state aid and a possible loss of federal Title I money.
watch_next: A revised sewer commission budget, which the commission said it would rebalance the following Tuesday and may bring back.
A public hearing on the Charter Review Committee draft on April 5 at 7 p.m.
